The PR changes the native macOS gateway endpoint resolver so local `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.auth.password` `${ENV_VAR}` templates resolve from the app environment or fall through to LaunchAgent credentials instead of being used literally.

PR surface: Other +138. Total +138 across 2 files.

I did not live-run the packaged macOS app in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(macos): skip unresolved dashboard auth templates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101286.

macOS OpenClaw.app could treat `gateway.auth.token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}"` as a literal local dashboard token when the GUI app environment did not contain that variable. That bypassed the LaunchAgent token fallback and produced a dashboard URL with an encoded placeholder fragment instead of a usable token.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Teach the local macOS auth resolver to recognize full `${ENV_VAR}` templates for `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.auth.password`.
- Resolve templates from the app process environment when available.
- If unresolved, return nil so the existing LaunchAgent snapshot fallback can supply the local token/password, and so unresolved placeholders are never embedded in the dashboard URL.
- Keep remote gateway config token/password behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users launching OpenClaw.app from Finder/Dock can recover when the gateway token only exists in the per-user LaunchAgent environment. The dashboard URL uses the resolved LaunchAgent token when available, or omits token auto-auth instead of passing a raw placeholder.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added `GatewayEndpointStoreTests` coverage for LaunchAgent fallback, app-env template resolution, unresolved-template omission from the dashboard URL, and password fallback.
- `cd apps/macos && swift test --parallel --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` was attempted locally, but current `origin/main` fails before tests execute under Apple Swift 6.2.4 with unrelated strict-concurrency diagnostics in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatTranscriptCache.swift` (`sending 'db' risks causing data races` at lines 1032 and 1050).
- `cd apps/macos && swift test --parallel --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests -Xswiftc -strict-concurrency=minimal` was also attempted and hit the same unrelated compile blocker.
